newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere B slide continues in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Solidere B slide continues in Beirut.

text.p: Solidere B shares fell on the Beirut Stock Exchange on Monday and brokers said a heavy supply of A shares would drag prices further down.
B shares fell to $10.5 from $11.375 while A shares were unchanged at $10.5. A shares were trading in heavy supply.
"I expect Solidere shares to trade at $10 on Tuesday," Carole Deeb of Credit Commercial et Foncier told Reuters. That would be their lowest level since they began trading in mid-1994.

The shares slid last week after a surge stimulated by the rise in the company's Global Depositary Receipts in London and an expected announcement of 2.5 cents dividend at the annual shareholders' meeting scheduled for May 27.
However, brokers said last week the meeting would lack a quorum.
Of the three listed banks, Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to $16.5 after falling last week to $16.25 from $17.25.
"The period of profit-taking in BLC is over. I expect the share to stabilise around its current price level, with an upward trend," Deeb said.
Bank of Beirut rose to $3.625 from $3.5625 on Friday. Banque Audi was unchanged at $20.
The LIBX bank index rose 3.37 percent to 141.32. The LISPI general index rose 0.62 percent to 87.07 and the BLOM general index fell 2.27 percent to 918.98.
A total 30,000 BOB shares changed hands in a block on the floor at $3.5625. A block of 5,000 BLC shares also traded on the BSE at $16.25.

Also traded in block, unchanged at $1.28125, were 150,000 shares of Ciments Libanais which announced a 2.4 cents dividend on Thursday but froze payment pending settlement of a $5 million dispute with the finance ministry over 1992 and 1993 taxes and penalties.
The company announced a 20 percent rise in after-tax profits in 1996 but a 7.899 billion Lebanese pounds provision for the tax and penalties caused a 33.5 percent fall in net profits.
Total BSE turnover was 345,151 shares for a value of $1,844,899 from 140,280 shares for a value of $1,317,272 on Thursday.
Pipemaker Eternit rose to $1.96875 from $1.875. There was no trade in the two other listed industrial companies: Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic.
